title: Adaptive SLO tiers for streaming first-token and per-token latency with tenant-priority routing
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem statement: Hosted streaming chat customers show divergent expectations: premium tenants require first-token latency and per-token tail guarantees (interactive feel) while lower-tier customers accept higher per-token latency for lower cost. We need an SLO framework that: 1) defines clear latency bands for first-token and steady-state per-token streaming, 2) ties routing/fast-path allocation to tenant priority, 3) specifies error budgets and burn-rate rules, and 4) provides rollout gates and contract tests to prevent regressions. Scope: Define SLO tiers (Premium / Standard / Economy) for both first-token (TTFT) and per-token delta latency, availability targets, and associated error budget policies. Define canary gating thresholds and rollback criteria. Exclude pricing changes and billing plumbing; infrastructure capacity procurement will be a separate Eng ticket. Goal: Have a PRD and a minimal acceptance checklist so ENG can implement routing + runtime knobs and Console can show per-tenant SLO status by release.
slo_definitions: Premium: first-token p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 220ms, p99 <= 400ms; per-token p50 <= 20ms, p95 <= 60ms; availability >= 99.95% monthly
Standard: first-token p50 <= 200ms, p95 <= 420ms, p99 <= 800ms; per-token p50 <= 40ms, p95 <= 120ms; availability >= 99.8% monthly
Economy: first-token p50 <= 450ms, p95 <= 900ms, p99 <= 1500ms; per-token p50 <= 100ms, p95 <= 300ms; availability >= 99.5% monthly
error_budget_policy: Calculate monthly error budget from availability target (100% - availability). Track burn-rate daily using rolling 6-hour and 24-hour windows.

High burn-rate (>3x expected for 6-hour window) triggers automated mitigations: reduce economy tenant fast-path allocations by 50%, enable model-variant fallback for standard tier, and page on-call if premium burn-rate >1.5x.

If monthly error budget for premium tier exhausted, immediately halt canary rollout and revert last model/infra change; begin incident postmortem and restrict risky experiments until budget recovers to 50%.

Economy tier may be softly degraded (increase batching, enable lower-precision quantized runtime) before standard/premium are affected. Any degradation must be surfaced in Console with clear customer-facing status messages.
rollout_gates: Canary stage: 1% traffic for 24h with premium p95 within 1.1x of baseline and no >2x increase in premium error-rate. Metric checks: first-token p95, per-token p95, 5xx rate, tail latency (>p99) count.
Staged ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 60% over 7 days. Advance only if canary and previous stage burn-rate <1.5x and no customer-impacting alerts in last 6 hours.

Automated abort: Any stage where premium p99 increases >30% vs baseline or premium availability drops below defined availability for that tier for >30 minutes triggers automatic rollback and mute of the rollout job.
Fallback policy: If capacity constraints observed, route new requests from Economy tier to best-effort pools and divert Standard to quantized model variants before touching Premium fast-path.
acceptance_criteria: PRD approved by Eng, SRE, and Console PMs
End-to-end test harness that simulates mixed-tenant traffic and measures first-token and per-token latencies at p50/p95/p99 included in CI
Canary gating automation implemented in deployment pipeline with checks defined above
Console shows per-tenant SLO status (current burn, remaining budget, last 24h trend) and exposes a link to recent CI contract test results
Runbook updated with clear mitigation steps for each burn-rate bracket and automated actions documented
Performance regression contract tests must fail the PR if premium first-token p95 degrades >5% vs baseline
monitoring_queries_and_alerts: Query: streaming.per_token.latency.p99{tier="premium"} - alert if trend increase >25% over 30m
Query: requests.5xx.rate{environment="prod"} - warn at 0.1% spike relative to hourly baseline
